title: HostConfig
description:
A host's `config.toml`. No key has a default: a key its section declares and the file
omits is refused by name, and so is a key no section declares. What may be absent is a whole
section — `[proxy]`, `[metrics]`, `[volumes.zerofs]` — and one that is present is filled in
completely.

artifacts.description: Where the layers a document names come from.

exports.description: Where a checkpoint goes when the document asks for it as a bundle.

filesystem.description: Absent is a host nothing can ask about a guest's files.

http_admission.description: Absent preserves unlimited concurrent HTTP requests. Changes require `nibrunnerd start`.

logs.description: Absent keeps the newest 256 MiB of each app's output.

max_apps.description:
How many apps this host is laid out for. Everything that counts slots follows from it:
the slot ring, the loopback ports reserved from 21000, the nbd minors on a zerofs host,
the kernel's conntrack table at 1024 entries an app, what the metrics page calls the
total. `install` measures what this machine holds and writes the least of memory, disk
and ports; `start` says the three against what is set.

max_concurrent_vm_starts.description: Optional host-wide bound on simultaneous VM boots and snapshot restores.

metrics.description: Absent is a host that scrapes nothing.

network.description: What a guest is denied, by name.

paths.description: Where this host keeps what is its own.

proxy.description: Absent serves nothing: no hostname, no raw port.

vm_budgets.description: Absent preserves VM processes without additional cgroup limits.

HttpAdmission.description: Optional limits on requests through the hostname router. Omission preserves unrestricted ingress.

app_concurrent.description: Default per-app limit. Aliases of an app share this capacity.

host_concurrent.description: Requests across all routed apps, including those waiting for a wake or streaming a body.

VmBudget.description: Optional host-enforced budgets for each Firecracker process, including its guest memory.

cpu_percent.description: 100 is one host CPU. This does not change the guest's vCPU count.

memory_mib.description: Includes guest RAM and Firecracker overhead. Exceeding it can kill the VM.

artifacts.description: One store, in S3 or on this disk.

exports.description: The store a bundle is put in, and the disk it is assembled on first.

staging_dir.description: A bundle is assembled here and removed after.

filesystem.description:
What a guest holds, listed on request over a socket on this machine. Nothing here is an
input: it answers reads, and what this host runs stays the document's to say.

socket.description:
Where the socket is put. Whoever may read it may list any app's files, so it belongs
somewhere only this host's own account can reach.

logs.description:
How much of each app's output stays on disk, under `paths.state_dir/logs`. Nothing on the
host reads it back: it is there to be tailed.

keep_mib_per_app.description:
Whole mebibytes, more than 0. The newest this many of an app's output, in two files:
`<appId>.log` becomes `<appId>.log.1` when it passes this, over the one before it, so
an app holds between one and two of these on disk however fast it writes. 256 is weeks
of an app that logs a line per request, and about a minute of one that floods.

metrics.description:
A Prometheus page, rendered from the same builder that writes `reported.json`. Nothing here
is an input.

port.description:
A free port, outside the range the slots take from 21000, other than `proxy.http.port`,
and not 9091 on a zerofs host, which ZeroFS holds.

network.description:
The ranges a guest is denied by name, on top of the blanket rules: public addresses that are
still yours, and that a tenant must not reach. Both may be empty; both must be there.

paths.description: Every one an absolute path, and every one this host's alone.

desired_state_file.description: The document this host watches and converges on.

runtime_dir.description: Sockets and pidfiles that outlive the daemon.

snapshot_dir.description: Where a sleeping app's memory goes. On a zerofs host it shares its disk with the cache.

versions_file.description: What `install` stamped what it laid down into, read back into `reported.json`.

proxy.description:
Every way in. Each section under here is absent or complete, and each binds an address of
its own, because each faces a different machine.

http.description: The one HTTP listener. Absent, a document naming a hostname is refused.

raw.description: Ports carried to a guest unread. Absent carries nothing raw.

proxy.http.description:
The one HTTP listener, where the edge reaches it. One per host: nothing here redirects, so a
plain port beside a TLS one would serve every app both ways forever.

port.description: A free port, outside the range the slots take from 21000. Not 0.

tls.description:
Serve the port encrypted. Absent is plain HTTP, which is what a host behind an edge that
terminates TLS wants.

proxy.http.tls.description:
One certificate for the whole host — there is no SNI selection, so a wildcard in practice —
read once, at startup. Obtaining and renewing it is certbot's or the edge's.

client_ca.description:
Makes a caller's own certificate the price of the handshake, which on an origin whose IP
is discoverable is what keeps it reachable only through the edge.

proxy.http.tls.client_ca.description: The certificates a caller may present, as a PEM trust pool.

certificate.description: PEM, holding every certificate the pool trusts.

proxy.raw.description:
Ports carried to a guest unread — ssh, DNS, WireGuard — reached at a port of their own,
tcp or udp, where the relay that publishes them reaches this host.

listen_address.description: An IP address to bind: a private one the relay can see, never the world's.

max_ports_per_guest.description: How many raw ports an app may name: 1 to 7, what a slot reserves past its HTTP port.

volumes.description: The backend, and the prefix every volume on this host is under.

backend.description:
`local-file` is sparse files under `paths.state_dir`, and no export. `zerofs` is blocks
in an object store, reached from the guest over NBD.

storage_prefix.description:
Where this host's volumes live under the store: 1 to 512 bytes, no leading or trailing
`/`, no empty, `.` or `..` segment. One host, not one app: every tenant here shares it,
and deleting it destroys all of them.

zerofs.description: Required by the `zerofs` backend, refused by `local-file`.

volumes.zerofs.description:
Everything `install` needs to lay ZeroFS down and everything the daemon needs to reach it
once systemd has it running. Its two configuration files are rendered from here.

cache_dir.description: The disk cache of the object store.

cache_disk_gib.description:
Whole gibibytes, more than 0. Size it against the disk it is on, which it shares with
`paths.snapshot_dir`: a full one breaks the filesystem every app on the host runs from.

cache_memory_gib.description: Whole gibibytes, more than 0. Held back from what any guest may be promised.

checkpoint_runtime_dir.description: Where the checkpoint reader an export starts keeps its socket.

mount_path.description: This host's own view of the filesystem.

nbd_socket_path.description: Where ZeroFS serves NBD, which is what a guest's disk is.

ninep_socket_path.description: Where ZeroFS serves 9P, which is how the host reaches the filesystem itself.
